title: The Lord's Day
definition: The Lord's Day is the first day of the week, associated with Christ's resurrection and the gathered worship of His people.
summary: The Lord's Day is the resurrection-shaped day of Christian worship, remembrance, and gathered devotion to Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ rose from the dead and is worshiped by His people as the living Lord.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine is distinct from gathering in general because it centers on the weekly rhythm shaped by Christ's resurrection. The Church marks time around the risen Lord, remembering that the new creation has dawned in Him. The Lord's Day trains believers to order life around worship rather than around productivity, entertainment, or self-rule.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because time reveals worship. A resurrection-shaped rhythm reminds the Church that Christ's victory is not an occasional theme but the center of Christian life. It gives believers a repeated mercy: a day to gather, remember, hear, rejoice, and reorient.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Prepare for the Lord's Day as a gift, not a burden. Use it to remember the resurrection, gather with God's people, and reset your heart around Christ. Where circumstances limit you, still seek a deliberate rhythm of worship and holy remembrance.
